what_its_for: This medicine helps treat upset stomach, heartburn, nausea, indigestion, and diarrhea. It coats the stomach lining to help soothe irritation and slow down loose stools.
how_to_take: You can take this medicine as a liquid, chewable tablet, or regular tablet. If you take the chewable tablets, chew them completely before swallowing — do not swallow them whole. Shake the liquid bottle well before each use. You can take it with or without food. Drink plenty of water while using this medicine, especially if you have diarrhea.
dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older: take 2 tablets or 30 mL (about 2 tablespoons) of liquid every 30 to 60 minutes as needed. Do not take more than 8 doses in one day (24 hours). For children under 12 years old, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before using, as dosing is based on the child's weight and age.
missed_dose: This medicine is usually taken only when you need it, not on a regular schedule. If your doctor has told you to take it at specific times and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue as normal. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep it out of the reach of children. Do not freeze the liquid form. Check the expiration date on the package and do not use it after that date.
what_to_avoid: Do not take this medicine if you are allergic to aspirin or other salicylates, or if you take blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin). Avoid taking it with other medications that contain salicylates, such as aspirin. Do not give this medicine to children or teenagers who have or are recovering from chickenpox or flu-like symptoms, as it may cause a rare but serious condition called Reye's syndrome. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine. Do not use it for more than 2 days unless your doctor tells you to.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical help right away if: your diarrhea lasts more than 2 days or gets worse; you have a fever above 101°F (38.3°C); you see blood or mucus in your stool; you notice ringing in your ears or hearing loss; you feel confused, very drowsy, or unusually tired; you develop an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have kidney disease before using this medicine.
when_it_works: This medicine usually starts to work within 30 to 60 minutes of taking it. You should notice less nausea, stomach discomfort, or diarrhea fairly quickly. Do not use it for longer than 2 days without talking to your doctor. Note: this medicine may make your tongue or stools look black or dark — this is harmless and normal, but let your doctor know if you are concerned.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it may not be safe, especially during the last three months of pregnancy. Children and teenagers: Do NOT give this medicine to children or teenagers who have chickenpox, flu, or flu-like symptoms due to the risk of Reye's syndrome. Always check with a doctor or pharmacist before giving it to children under 12. Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to this medication. Kidney disease: Avoid or use with extra caution if you have kidney problems, since the salicylate in this medicine can build up in your body.
